title: Binary Ghost
summary: A real ELF binary hides an XOR-encrypted payload. Reverse it to recover the flag.
briefing:
Malware analysis recovered a Linux binary ("beacon") from a compromised host. It is a real 64-bit ELF executable. Inside, a decrypt routine un-scrambles an embedded payload using a single-byte XOR before the beacon transmits it.

Analyse the binary with your own tools:
- "file beacon" confirms the format
- "strings beacon" reveals the XOR key and other artifacts
- "objdump -d beacon" (or Ghidra / radare2 / GDB) shows the decrypt loop in the .text section
- The encrypted payload sits in the .rodata section

Extract the encrypted bytes from .rodata and XOR each one with the key you found. The result is the flag.

(Note: the binary is not meant to be executed — analyse it statically.)
objectives: Recover the XOR key from strings / disassembly
Locate the encrypted payload in the .rodata section
XOR-decode it to recover the flag

hints.title: Find the key
hints.text: Run: strings beacon | grep -i xor — the key is printed as "XOR key: 0x5a". Confirm it in the disassembly (mov al,0x5a).

hints.title: Extract .rodata
hints.text: Dump the read-only data: objdump -s -j .rodata beacon. The printable strings come first; the encrypted flag bytes follow them. XOR each byte with 0x5a.

artifacts.description: Recovered 64-bit ELF binary. Analyse statically — do not run it.
